churn_resistance.rationale: Data access, formatting and config are well isolated and the server/Vite wiring mirrors the starters (so a framework upgrade touches almost nothing), but the build-time stub detection depends on an undocumented internal string duplicated in five places, one route misses it entirely, and the total absence of TypeScript checking means the pervasive any casts are never validated.

findings.issue: Build-time render detection compares url.hostname to the literal 'gracile-static', an undocumented internal constant of the engine's render pass (packages/engine/src/routes/render.ts), duplicated verbatim in five route handlers (also pokemon/[name].ts:104, moves/[name].ts:28, abilities/[name].ts:19, types/[name].ts:24). If the framework renames the stub host or stops invoking handlers at build, every handler would silently start fetching the live API during vite build (or break the build).
findings.suggestion: Extract one helper (e.g. in app/src/lib/api.ts or a lib/build-mode.ts: isBuildStub(url)) and route all handlers through it; add a comment citing the engine source so the assumption is visible and greppable.

findings.issue: Unlike the other five routes, the /types handler has no build-stub guard, so vite build issues a real HTTP fetch to the API; the production build fails when the API is unreachable and build-time data fetching contradicts the spec's request-time-data requirement.
findings.suggestion: Apply the same centralized build-stub short-circuit used by the other routes (return { types: [] } when the stub host is detected).

findings.issue: No tsconfig.json, no typescript/@types/node devDependencies and no check script, so the .ts sources are transpiled by Vite but never type-checked; the official Gracile starter ships a tsconfig extending @gracile/gracile/tsconfigs/strictest plus a `tsc` check script.
findings.suggestion: Add { "extends": "@gracile/gracile/tsconfigs/strictest" } and a `check` script running tsc, with typescript and @types/node as devDependencies.

findings.issue: context.props.GET is cast to any in every template (also index.ts:164, moves/[name].ts:58, abilities/[name].ts:49, types/[name].ts:52, types/index.ts:22) and API payloads are any (e.g. species: any at [name].ts:106), so defineRoute's typed-props inference — the framework's main churn-protection — is bypassed and API shape drift is invisible until render time.
findings.suggestion: Define response interfaces in lib/api.ts (or per-route types) and let the handlers return literal objects so props types flow to template contexts without casts.

findings.issue: Server-side fetches have no timeout or AbortController; a slow or hung upstream stalls the SSR response (and the build-time render) indefinitely.
findings.suggestion: Pass AbortSignal.timeout(ms) to fetch, with the timeout exposed as a constant next to API_BASE.

findings.issue: Global CSS is served raw from public/ via an absolute link, bypassing the Vite pipeline the framework sits on: no minification, no content-hashed filenames, and an extra @import request for tokens.css (global.css:1).
findings.suggestion: Link the stylesheet by source path (e.g. /src/styles/global.css) or import it in the document route so Vite fingerprints and minifies it, matching Gracile's documented asset pattern.

findings.issue: `dev: vite` runs the bare Vite dev server, so dev and production diverge: the express wiring in server.js (static assets + adapter) never runs in development. Current 0.11 supports `gracile({ server: { entry: './server.js' } })`, which bridges the user's server as middleware in dev and bundles it in build.
findings.suggestion: Consider server: { entry: './server.js' } in vite.config.ts so one file owns server wiring with dev/prod parity; the current split also works and is the documented default, so this is optional.

summary: The app is built entirely on the current stable Gracile (0.11.0) APIs and mirrors the official starter wiring, with four lean, up-to-date dependencies and a genuine platform-first slant (fetch, URL/URLSearchParams, native form controls, plain CSS custom properties). Its main age risks are the five copies of an undocumented internal hostname used to dodge build-time handler invocation, one route (/types) that misses the guard and therefore fetches live data during vite build, and a complete absence of TypeScript checking that leaves the pervasive any casts unvalidated. Centralizing the build-stub detection and adding the framework's own tsconfig plus a tsc check would make the codebase substantially more upgrade-proof.
